title: VideoBrief
description: The machine-readable part of a GitHub issue that asks for a video. A brief lives as a fenced ```brief YAML block inside the issue body, so an issue stays something a human writes in one sitting while still being something a tool can execute. It carries ONLY what the owner authored: what footage to use, what music, who is on screen, and what goes on their nameplate. It never carries a derived field -- clean, footage_tier, traversal_hero and casting are computed by tools/derive.py at assembly time, and a brief that sets one is an error by the same rule that governs a tagger. It also never carries a guess: an unknown character id is rejected rather than normalized, because `character` names a real person via vocab/casting.yaml and a wrong value credits somebody for a shot they are not in.

title.description: Working title for the finished cut. Free text -- this is the owner's name for the piece, not an id.

sources.description: Source footage the cut may draw from, in the order the owner wants it considered. An entry is a YouTube URL plus, once the video has been ingested, the index video_id that tools/ingest.py assigned it. A brief may name footage that is not indexed yet: that is the normal starting state, and it is what tells an agent an indexing pass is needed first.

characters.description: Lead character ids the cut is about, as canonical keys of `leads.values` in vocab/casting.yaml (or any of that entry's `aka` spellings, which normalize to the canonical key). This is the SAME vocabulary the segment index uses for `character`, so a brief and a search agree on who a name refers to. An id that is not in vocab/casting.yaml is rejected: adding a character is a vocabulary edit, and casting one to a real person is an owner decision.

plates.description: Nameplates the owner wants on screen, with the copy they authored. Copy appears here only when it is not already on a binding in vocab/casting.yaml -- the normal path is that a plate names a `character` and tools/plate.py reads that binding's `plate:` block. Copy in a brief is the owner speaking, which is the one source that may introduce a new claim about a real person.

beats.description: Owner direction pinned to a point or range in a source, in the owner's own words -- 'cut out the closeups of Saladin's face', 'this is the maximum hero shot'. Kept as free text on purpose: this is intent, and flattening it into an enum would lose the part an editor actually needs.

notes.description: Anything that does not fit a field above -- tone, pacing, references. Free text.

automatable.description: Whether an agent can finish this work unattended. REQUIRED, because in this repo three classes of work are permanently not automatable -- a visual judgement about a frame, a claim about a real person, and a licensing decision -- and an agent that stops at one of them has succeeded, not failed. 'no' means the issue is waiting on the owner and an agent should say exactly what it needs and stop; 'partly' means the mechanical half can be done now and the remainder named.

blocked_on.description: When `automatable` is 'no' or 'partly', the exact decision or input that is missing, addressed to the person who can supply it. A brief that stops without naming what would unblock it makes the next agent rediscover the blocker.

url.description: YouTube watch URL of the source footage.

video_id.description: Index id for this source (videos/<video_id>.json), once it has been ingested. Absent means the footage is not in the index yet.

in.description: Where the usable material starts, mm:ss or HH:MM:SS. Absent means the start of the video.

out.description: Where the usable material ends. Absent means the end of the video.

note.description: Why this source is here, or what to take from it.

source.description: One piece of source footage. Needs a `url` or a `video_id`: an entry with neither names nothing.

url.description: Where the track can be found. The repo indexes music the same way it indexes footage: by reference, never by committing the audio.

title.description: Track name, when the URL alone does not say it.

path.description: Path under media/ for an already-fetched track, e.g. media/deutschland_instrumental.mp3. Gitignored like all media.

note.description: How the track should sit against the picture -- mood, where the drop lands, what to cut to.

music.description: The music bed. A cut scored to a specific track is a different edit from the same shots scored to another, so the track belongs in the brief rather than being chosen at render time.

plate.description: One nameplate. Either it names a `character` whose copy already lives on a binding in vocab/casting.yaml, or it carries owner-authored `copy`. The field set of `copy` is CLOSED and mirrors the reference deck (docs/skills/plates.md): inventing a row the deck has no field for is the thing this schema exists to prevent.

at.description: Where the plate should land, in source time. A reveal is a timing decision the owner often makes ('drop her nameplate right after she removes her helmet, 0:14'), so it is carried rather than re-derived.

video_id.description: Which source `at` refers to, when the brief names more than one.

character.description: Lead character id this plate credits, validated against vocab/casting.yaml exactly as `characters` is.

note.description: Direction about the plate that is not copy -- e.g. 'again here, as a contributor'.

plateCopy.description: On-screen nameplate copy, in the reference deck's closed field set. Same shape as a `plate:` block in vocab/casting.yaml, because it is the same thing: the copy tools/plate.py renders. Every row here is a claim about a real person, so it is owner-authored or absent -- never inferred from a photograph, a GitHub profile, or a resemblance.

label.description: The uppercase eyebrow, e.g. 'TRUSTEE // GUARDIAN' or 'MAINTAINER // GUARDIAN'.

class.description: Subclass and class, e.g. 'Voidwalker Warlock'. Every class row in the deck is '<Subclass> <Class>'; a bare class is one word short and is the defect issue #5 records.

name.description: The person's name as they are credited.

title.description: The seal line, e.g. 'Reconciler of the Plane'.

kind.description: Which shape of card this is. 'ghost' drops the class row, because a Ghost has no subclass.

variant.description: The gold leader treatment. Takes precedence over `trustee`, mirroring the CSS.

at.description: Point or range start in the source this direction is about.

to.description: End of the range, when the direction covers one.

video_id.description: Which source `at` refers to, when the brief names more than one.

note.description: The direction itself, in the owner's words.

timecode.description: mm:ss or HH:MM:SS, the same shape as segment.start_tc, so a brief and the index share a clock.
